This appeal coming on for orders this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER
No one is appearing from respondents side from long time.

The present appeal is admitted on 28.04.2011 and disposed of today by the following order:-
1.

This appeal has been filed being aggrieved by the award dated 12.05.2010 passed in Claim Case No. 553/2008, whereby the learned IInd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandla (M.P.) has given a compensation of Rs. 5,000/- under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 to appellant/claimant Sarita Bai.

entities.text: IInd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandla (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Appeal has been filed on the ground that on 12.05.2008 at about 2 O'clock in Shanti Nagar,
Nainpur Distt. Mandla, non- applicant No. 1, Munna while driving the Tractor No. MP-22 H-5958 of respondent No. 2, Kunjilal, rashly and negligently due to which the claimant, who was riding the tractor as a labourer fell down and wheel of the tractor passed over the left leg of the claimant resulting into serious injury and ultimately permanent disability to the claimant.
She was treated at hospital at Nainpur, Mandla and Jabalpur.

It is further submitted that after her discharge from Mandla, Hospital she lodged Ex. P-1 FIR on 07.08.2010 because the respondent did not report the accident and misguided her, criminal - 3 - case was also registered against respondent No. 1 and he was convicted in Criminal Case No.
233/2008 on 30.09.2008 for that accident.
It is further submitted that appellant underwent long treatment for upto 3 months.
She has sustained permanent scar and deformity over left thigh with shortening of leg along with discomforts as examined by P.W. 2, Dr. Bansor, Govt. Hospital Banda.
Therefore, her physical fitness, fame, beauty and capacity of working and earning has affected.
She has continuous trouble in walking, therefore, she filed a claim for compensation.

The award of the Tribunal allowing Rs. 5,000/- compensation is totally inadequate, therefore, enhancement of Rs.
6,28,900/- along with 12 percent interest is demanded.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant, during course of argument referred to the following citations :-
1. Sunita and ors. vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and anr. 2020 (13)
SCC 486, in which in para 20, it is mentioned that a well reasoned award of the Tribunal cannot be reversed by taking hyper- technical approach and demanding proof beyond reasonable doubt.
2. S. Parumal vs. K. Ambika and ors. 2015 (11) SCC 411 in which in Para 14 it has been laid down that Sarita Bai vs Munna @ Girdhari Lal on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24518166/
2 - 4 - injured/claimant is to be compensated for his permanent disability and for loss of earning due to inability.
3.

sentences.text:
"Thus in view of the aforesaid enunciation of law, the appeals which are filed in respect of the claims instituted before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal before 2.4.2008, fixed court fee would be payable whereas in respect of the appeal against the awards in respect of claims filed on or after 2.4.2008 ad-valorem court fee as provided under the Act No.6 of 2008 would be payable."
4.
This appeal has been filed on 24.07.2010, therefore, court fees would be payable.
The appellant has paid the court fees of Rs. 6,250/-.
Appeal is for enhancement of Rs. 6,28,900/-.
Perused the record and the award dated 12.05.2010 passed by IInd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandla in Claim Case No. 553/2008.

entities.text: IInd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandla
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On perusal of the photographs, it is seen that left leg right from - 5 - knee to upper portion has been badly damaged which would certainly hamper the working/earning capacity of the claimant along with discomfort, pain, suffering, future treatment and other enjoyment of life

, therefore, the amount awarded by the Tribunal for Rs.5,000/- seems very less,
even otherwise it is not a case of dismissal and after considering all facts, claim has not been dismissed that it is a fraudulent claim, therefore, treating the injury of claimant of grievous nature and not simple nature as held by the learned Tribunal and consequently for loss of earning, physical and mental pain and future treatment, the award of compensation of amount of Rs. 2,40,000/-.
5.
Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed off.

6. Let a copy of this order be sent to the concerned court along with record.
